title: opensandbox-group/OpenSandbox — Secure, Fast, and Extensible Sandbox runtime for AI agents.
content:
Run AI agents in sandboxes on your own infrastructure.
OpenSandbox gives AI applications isolated environments to execute code, run commands, manage files, and operate browsers or desktops. Start locally with Docker and deploy on Kubernetes through a unified sandbox API.
Quick Start · Examples · Documentation · Fast Sandbox
Requirements:
- Docker (required for local execution)
- Python 3.10+ (required for examples and local runtime)
uvx opensandbox-server init-config ~/.sandbox.toml --example docker
uvx opensandbox-server
# Show help
# uvx opensandbox-server -h
Install the Sandbox SDK
uv pip install opensandbox
Create a sandbox from an alpine image and execute commands and scripts.
import asyncio
from opensandbox import Sandbox
from opensandbox.models import WriteEntry
async def main() -> None:
    # 1. Create a sandbox from the alpine image
    sandbox = await Sandbox.create("alpine")
    try:
        # 2. Execute a shell command
        execution = await sandbox.commands.run("echo 'Hello OpenSandbox!'")
        print(execution.logs.stdout[0].text)
        # 3. Write a script file
        await sandbox.files.write_files([
            WriteEntry(
                path="/tmp/hello.sh",
                data="echo \"Hello $1\"\necho '2 + 2 =' $((2 + 2))",
                mode=755,
            )
        ])
        # 4. Read the file back
        content = await sandbox.files.read_file("/tmp/hello.sh")
        print(f"Content: {content}")
        # 5. Execute the script
        execution = await sandbox.commands.run("sh /tmp/hello.sh OpenSandbox")
        for log in execution.logs.stdout:
            print(log.text)
    finally:
        # 6. Cleanup the sandbox
        await sandbox.destroy()
if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())
Explore examples by what you want your agent to do. Runnable source code lives in examples/.
See the full example catalog for more coding agents, framework integrations, remote development environments, Kubernetes deployment, and storage patterns.
Pick your language:
Python
pip install opensandbox
Java/Kotlin (Gradle Kotlin DSL)
dependencies {
    implementation("com.alibaba.opensandbox:sandbox:{latest_version}")
}
Java/Kotlin (Maven)
<dependency>
    <groupId>com.alibaba.opensandbox</groupId>
    <artifactId>sandbox</artifactId>
    <version>{latest_version}</version>
</dependency>
JavaScript/TypeScript
npm install @alibaba-group/opensandbox
C#/.NET
dotnet add package Alibaba.OpenSandbox
Go
go get github.com/alibaba/OpenSandbox/sdks/sandbox/go
OpenSandbox also provides osb, a terminal CLI for the common sandbox workflow: create sandboxes, run commands, move files, inspect diagnostics, and manage runtime egress policy.
Install:
pip install opensandbox-cli
# or
uv tool install opensandbox-cli
Quick start:
osb config init
osb config set connection.domain localhost:8080
osb config set connection.protocol http
osb config set connection.api_key <your-api-key>
osb sandbox create --image python:3.12 --timeout 30m -o json
osb command run <sandbox-id> -o raw -- python -c "print(1 + 1)"
See the CLI README for the full command reference.
The OpenSandbox MCP server exposes sandbox creation, command execution, and text file operations to MCP-capable clients such as Claude Code and Cursor.
Install and run:
pip install opensandbox-mcp
opensandbox-mcp --domain localhost:8080 --protocol http
Minimal stdio config:
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "opensandbox": {
      "command": "opensandbox-mcp",
      "args": ["--domain", "localhost:8080", "--protocol", "http"]
    }
  }
}
See the MCP README for client-specific setup.
OpenSandbox release images are published under the same component name in three official registries:
- Docker Hub: docker.io/opensandbox/<component>
- GitHub Container Registry: ghcr.io/opensandbox-group/opensandbox/<component>
- Alibaba Cloud Container Registry: sandbox-registry.cn-zhangjiakou.cr.aliyuncs.com/opensandbox/<component>
Pin production images by digest and check the release verification guide for signing coverage before deployment. Legacy per-component releases support Cosign signatures and provenance attestations; current umbrella releases have a tracked signing and provenance gap and must not be assumed to provide the same verification evidence.

report.summary: OpenSandbox is an Apache-2.0, self-hosted runtime that gives AI agents isolated Docker or Kubernetes sandboxes for code, commands, files, browsers, and desktops via a unified API.
report.background: AI agents are moving from chat to action: writing code, running shell commands, editing files, and driving browsers or desktops. Executing that work directly on a developer machine or production host creates serious security and reliability risks, so teams increasingly want disposable, isolated environments. OpenSandbox targets that need with a self-hosted sandbox layer that starts locally with Docker and scales to Kubernetes through one API. The project is part of the Agentic AI Foundation and is licensed under Apache 2.0. Its package namespaces and registry options point to close ties with Alibaba’s ecosystem, while the multi-language SDKs and MCP server aim to fit existing agent frameworks and coding assistants rather than lock users into a single stack.
key_points: OpenSandbox provides one sandbox API that works locally with Docker and in production on Kubernetes. Developers can create a sandbox from an image, run commands or scripts, write and read files, and destroy the environment when finished. The README includes a short Python example showing the full lifecycle.

The project ships SDKs for Python, Java/Kotlin, JavaScript/TypeScript, C#/.NET, and Go, plus an osb terminal CLI. The CLI covers creating sandboxes, running commands, moving files, checking diagnostics, and managing runtime egress policy, which makes it useful for scripts and day-to-day operations.

An MCP server exposes sandbox creation, command execution, and text-file operations to MCP-capable clients such as Claude Code and Cursor. That lets coding agents use OpenSandbox as an execution backend without custom glue code, though users still need to run and secure the server.

Release images are published to Docker Hub, GitHub Container Registry, and Alibaba Cloud Container Registry. The documentation advises pinning production images by digest and checking verification coverage. It also warns that current umbrella releases have a signing and provenance gap, unlike legacy per-component releases.

OpenSandbox is positioned as a project of the Agentic AI Foundation under Apache 2.0. The repository links architecture, deployment, API, credential vault, roadmap, and enhancement-proposal docs, indicating an effort to build a broader sandbox ecosystem rather than a single-purpose tool.
report.impact: OpenSandbox matters because isolation is becoming a core layer for agent platforms. A self-hosted, multi-language sandbox API can reduce lock-in and give enterprises more control over where agent code and data run. For developers, it lowers the barrier to safely executing generated code and integrating with MCP clients, but it also adds operational work: running Docker or Kubernetes, managing API keys, patching images, and handling the documented signing gap. For regular users, the main benefit is safer agent behavior: code runs in a disposable environment instead of on a personal machine. It does not remove the need for careful permissions, network egress controls, and review before production deployment.
report.tools: Start with the OpenSandbox repository and quick start: uvx opensandbox-server init-config, then the Python SDK or osb CLI. Try opensandbox-mcp with Claude Code or Cursor to connect agents to a local server. For deployment, review the Kubernetes guide, image registries, and release-verification notes. Also watch related isolation projects such as E2B, Daytona, gVisor, and Firecracker for comparison.
